title: Make ThreatDetector target-, weapon-, and disarm-aware and remove duplicate scan in plan-manager.ts

sections.what: Upgrade ThreatDetector to account for visible held weapons, event target attribution (who threatens whom), observer relationship affinity toward the holder, and disarm/drop de-escalation, and remove the stale duplicate threat scan in static/js/agent/plan-manager.ts.
sections.why: static/js/agent/threat-detector.ts checks otherPlayer.traits.hostile, closeness < -20, and whether person.name appeared as actor of action === 'attack', blindly labeling that actor 'hostile toward you'. In multi-party confrontations where an ally disarms an aggressor (or briefly holds a weapon), ThreatDetector either ignores armed state altogether or falsely flags the intervening ally as hostile toward the observer and locks turns in danger even after the weapon is dropped/disarmed. Meanwhile static/js/agent/plan-manager.ts (lines 221-237) duplicates an older loop omitting turnEvents. (Note: the separate attack vs combat turn-event string mismatch across ThreatDetector, _vitalsScene, and interrupts.py is tracked in its own dedicated bug.)
sections.how: 1. Extend threat evaluation in static/js/agent/threat-detector.ts to inspect: (a) who the target of any violent turnEvent is (actor -> target, normalized across 'combat', 'attack', and 'disarm'), (b) visible held weapons/hazards from players_in_area (blocked_by bug-588) vs unarmed disarm/restraint actions, (c) observer closeness/trust toward the holder (an ally holding a disarmed weapon creates alarm/context without falsely labeling the ally 'hostile toward you'), and (d) de-escalation events (drop, disarm, throw, release).\n2. Remove the duplicated hostile-actor scan in static/js/agent/plan-manager.ts (lines 221-237) that omits turnEvents so plan invalidation delegates cleanly to ThreatDetector.\n3. Add JS unit tests covering friend-disarming-aggressor standoffs, visible held firearm escalation, third-party hostility toward bystanders, and post-disarm/drop de-escalation.
sections.verify:
1. Run npm run build:ts and node tools/unit/run.cjs with ThreatDetector unit tests covering visible held weapons, target-specific attacks, ally disarming third party, and post-drop/throw de-escalation.
2. Verify plan-manager.ts no longer duplicates its own narrower threat loop.

acceptance.text: ThreatDetector distinguishes armed posture and event target (actor vs target) plus observer relationship affinity instead of treating every attack/disarm event or negative closeness as indiscriminate hostility toward charName.

Armed weapons visibly held by nearby actors (from bug-588 players_in_area holding data) escalate threat context accurately and distinguish an ally intervening/disarming a third aggressor from an attack aimed at charName.

Dropping, throwing, or disarming the weapon or switching to non-hostile post-resolution turnEvents downgrades or clears the immediate danger alert cleanly rather than locking subsequent calm turns in IMMEDIATE DANGER.
Duplicated hostile-actor scan in static/js/agent/plan-manager.ts (lines 221-237) is removed in favor of calling ThreatDetector so plan invalidation and decide threats share one rule set.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Turn Modal DECIDE/PLAN prompt header alert (`IMMEDIATE DANGER`) and Event Stream turn log.

Current availability: ThreatDetector in static/js/agent/threat-detector.ts runs a 4-line flat scan over traits.hostile, closeness < -20, and turnEvents attack actor while plan-manager.ts duplicates a narrower version without turnEvents.

Manual verification steps:
1. Run a scene where NPC C attacks NPC B or brandishes a weapon toward B while NPC B (close ally of A) disarms C and drops/throws the weapon.
2. Inspect A's DECIDE/PLAN prompts during the standoff and on the following turn after disarming.
   - expected: During the standoff, A sees accurate target- and weapon-aware threat framing (distinguishing the aggressor from ally B holding a disarmed weapon); after disarm/drop, the immediate danger lock clears cleanly.
